samples: This command-line tool prints a directory tree for the folder given as the first argument (or the current folder if none is given), with one line per file or folder showing its name and its size in bytes, indented two spaces per level and sorted by name within each folder. A folder's size is the total of every file beneath it, and anything that is neither a file nor a folder counts as zero bytes. It only needs console output, command-line arguments and read access to the filesystem, so it cannot write files or use the network, but one unreadable entry anywhere makes the whole run fail with a file error, and deeply nested trees are scanned repeatedly because each line re-measures everything beneath it.
